lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Hi David.
lines.translation: 嗨，戴维。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I haven't seen you in class for almost two weeks.
lines.translation: 我快两周没在课堂上见到你了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: We thought you had disappeared on holiday early or something.
lines.translation: 我们还以为你提早休假去哪里了呢。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Hi, Sarah.
lines.translation: 嗨，莎拉。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, it's a bit of a long story I'm afraid.
lines.translation: 唉，说来话长。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I got a throat infection last week and had to go to the hospital to get some antibiotics as I really wasn't getting any better.
lines.translation: 我上周喉咙感染了，因为病情实在不见好转，不得不去医院开了一些抗生素。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Oh yeah.
lines.translation: 哦，是的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: There have been so many viruses going around this winter.
lines.translation: 今年冬天有好多病毒在传播。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The weather has been so awful for the last few weeks.
lines.translation: 过去几周的天气真是太糟了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And, on the way back from the hospital, I slipped on some ice and fell and then had to go to the hospital to get an X-ray because I basically thought I broke my wrist, although, thankfully, it's not broken.
lines.translation: 还有，在从医院回来的路上，我在冰上滑倒摔了一跤，结果又得去医院拍 X 光，因为我以为自己把手腕给摔断了，不过幸好没断。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But I need to be careful with it for the next few weeks.
lines.translation: 但接下来的几周我得小心对待这只手。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Oh, that's too bad!
lines.translation: 哦，那太糟糕了！

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: How unfortunate!
lines.translation: 真是太倒霉了！

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: To make things worse, I managed to fall right in front of four girls from the ninth grade.
lines.translation: 更糟糕的是，我偏偏摔在了四个九年级女生面前。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So I was utterly humiliated.
lines.translation: 简直丢脸丢到家了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Plus, the laptop in my bag was broken too.
lines.translation: 而且，我包里的笔记本电脑也摔坏了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: No, what a complete catastrophe!
lines.translation: 天啊，这真是彻头彻尾的灾难！

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Is the laptop still under warranty?
lines.translation: 笔记本电脑还在保修期内吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If it is, then you can easily send it back to the manufacturer, and they'll send you a brand-new one for free surely.
lines.translation: 如果是的话，你就可以很方便地寄回给厂家，他们肯定会免费给你寄一台全新的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The warranty ran out three days before I broke it.
lines.translation: 保修期在我摔坏它的前三天就过了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And all my essays are in there, and I need to hand them in before we break for the Christmas holidays.
lines.translation: 我所有的论文都在里面，而且我必须在放圣诞假之前把它们交上去。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Listen, I have the number of a really good, affordable computer repair shop at home.
lines.translation: 听我说，我家里有一家又好又实惠的电脑维修店的电话。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: My dad has used this guy before and he can work miracles.
lines.translation: 我爸爸以前找过这个人，他简直能创造奇迹。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Let's go back to my house and we can call the repair shop, and you can have some tea and cookies too.
lines.translation: 我们回我家吧，我们可以给维修店打电话，你还可以喝点茶、吃点饼干。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Wow, thanks, Sarah!
lines.translation: 哇，谢谢你，莎拉！

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That would be great!
lines.translation: 那太好了！

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Let me just call my mom and let her know I'll be home a little bit later.
lines.translation: 我先给我妈妈打个电话，跟她说一声我会晚一点回家。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What does Sarah say she is going to do?
lines.translation: 莎拉说她会怎么做?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Conversation two.
lines.translation: 对话二

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Welcome to this week's episode of Book Talk.
lines.translation: 欢迎收听本周的《图书谈》。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: With me today is Heidi Brown, a historian who has written five critically acclaimed books about military history.
lines.translation: 今天和我一起做节目的是海蒂·布朗，她是一位历史学家，已经写了五本广受评论界好评的军事史著作。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Thanks for having me, John.
lines.translation: 谢谢你邀请我，约翰。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I'm so excited to talk about my latest book, which was published last month.
lines.translation: 我非常高兴能聊聊我的最新著作，这本书上个月刚刚出版。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So this book is a novel, your first attempt at that genre.
lines.translation: 所以，这本书是一部小说，是你第一次尝试这一体裁。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I thought it was a bit of a departure for you.
lines.translation: 我觉得这对你来说是一个不小的转变。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I'd say it's a major departure as it's not just a work of fiction.
lines.translation: 我想这是个重大起飞 因为它不只是虚构的作品

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's set 200 years in the future.
lines.translation: 未来有200年了

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Right.
lines.translation: 好。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So how did that happen?
lines.translation: 那么这是怎么发生的？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You spent three decades writing about the past and focusing on the 18th and 19th centuries.
lines.translation: 你花了三十年时间写过去的历史，重点关注十八世纪和十九世纪。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And now you're speculating about the future.
lines.translation: 现在却开始推测未来。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, after years of researching soldiers and chronicling their lives during battle, I just started wondering about other facets of their lives, especially their personal lives.
lines.translation: 嗯，多年来研究士兵并记录他们在战斗中的生活之后，我开始思考他们生活中的其他方面，尤其是他们的私人生活。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I can see that.
lines.translation: 我能理解。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Your novel is about soldiers and it focuses on their relationships, especially the bond between sons and mothers and men and their wives.
lines.translation: 你的小说写的是士兵，重点讲述他们之间的关系，尤其是儿子与母亲之间的感情，以及男人与妻子之间的联系。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Yes.
lines.translation: 是的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That focus came about when I still intended to write another book of history.
lines.translation: 我最初打算再写一本历史书时，就产生了这个关注点。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I started by researching soldiers' actual personal lives, studying their letters home.
lines.translation: 我先研究士兵真实的私人生活，研读他们寄回家的信件。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So how did that history book become a novel?
lines.translation: 那么，这本历史书后来是怎么变成小说的？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, I realized that the historical record was incomplete.
lines.translation: 嗯，我意识到历史记录并不完整。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So I'd either have to leave a lot of gaps or make a lot more assumptions than a historian should.
lines.translation: 所以，我要么得留下许多空白，要么就得做出远超历史学家应有程度的大量推断。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But why write a novel set in the future when your credentials are perfect for a historical novel?
lines.translation: 但既然你的资历非常适合写历史小说，为什么要写一部以未来为背景的小说呢？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: As a historian, any historical novel you write would have a lot of credibility.
lines.translation: 作为一名历史学家，无论你写什么历史小说，都会很有可信度。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I felt too constrained working with the past, like what I wrote needed to be fact as opposed to fiction, but writing about the future gave me more freedom to imagine, to invent.
lines.translation: 我觉得创作过去的题材束缚太多了，好像我写的东西必须是事实，而不能是虚构。但写未来让我有更多自由去想象和创造。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, having read your book, I'm glad you made that choice to move into fiction.
lines.translation: 读过你的书之后，我很高兴你做出了转向小说创作的选择。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题5到8是基于你刚才听到的谈话

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.translation: 5 个

lines.text: What does the man say about the woman?
lines.translation: 男人怎么说女人?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question 6.
lines.translation: 问题6

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What does the woman say about her newly published book?
lines.translation: 女人怎么说她的新出版的书?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question 7.
lines.translation: 问题7

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What did the woman do before writing her new book?
lines.translation: 那个女人写新书之前做了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question 8.
lines.translation: 问题8

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What does the woman say about her writing history books?
lines.translation: 她写历史书时怎么说?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Section B, directions.
lines.translation: B节,方向。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In this section you'll hear two passages.
lines.translation: 在这段里你会听到两段

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: At the end of each passage you'll hear three or four questions.
lines.translation: 每条路的尽头 你会听到三四个问题

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
lines.translation: 发言的通过和提问将只讲一次。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
lines.translation: 在听到一个问题后,你必须从四个选择中选择最好的答案,这四个选择分别是A、B、C和D。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
lines.translation: 在答题单单行的答题表一中标出相应的字母。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Whether it's in the hands of animated polar bears or Santa Claus, there's one thing you'll find in nearly all ads for Coca-Cola: the characteristic glass bottle.
lines.translation: 无论是由动画片中的北极熊还是圣诞老人拿着，在几乎所有可口可乐的广告中，你都会看到同一样东西：那只独具特色的玻璃瓶。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Most Americans don't drink soda out of the glass bottles seen in Coke's ads anymore.
lines.translation: 如今，大多数美国人已经不再用可口可乐广告中出现的玻璃瓶喝汽水了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But this week, the company is celebrating a century of the bottle that's been sold in more than 200 countries.
lines.translation: 但本周，这家公司正在庆祝这种已在全球200多个国家销售的瓶子问世一百周年。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Flash back to 1915, when a bottle of Coca-Cola cost just a nickel.
lines.translation: 回到1915年，那时一瓶可口可乐只要5美分。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: As the soft drink gained in popularity, it faced a growing number of competitors—counterfeits even trying to copy Coke's logo.
lines.translation: 随着这种软饮料越来越受欢迎，它面临的竞争者也越来越多，甚至还有仿冒品试图复制可口可乐的标志。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So, according to Coca-Cola historian Ted Ryan, the company decided to come up with packaging that couldn't be duplicated.
lines.translation: 因此，据可口可乐历史学家特德·瑞安介绍，公司决定设计一种无法仿制的包装。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: A product request was sent to eight different glass makers.
lines.translation: 公司向八家不同的玻璃制造商发出了一份产品设计要求。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Workers at the Root Glass Company got the request and began flipping through the encyclopedia at the local library, landing on cocoa seed.
lines.translation: 鲁特玻璃公司的工人收到要求后，开始在当地的图书馆翻阅百科全书，最后注意到了可可种子。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Though cocoa seed is not an ingredient of the soda, they designed their bottle based on the seed's shape and large middle.
lines.translation: 虽然可可种子并不是这种汽水的原料，但他们根据种子的形状和中部较大的特点设计了瓶子。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It won over Coke executives in Atlanta and would go on to receive its own trademark, spur collections and earn Coca-Cola an iconic image that made it part of American culture for a century.
lines.translation: 这一设计赢得了亚特兰大可口可乐公司高管的认可，后来还获得了自己的商标，推动了收藏热潮，并为可口可乐赢得了一个具有标志性的形象，使其在一个世纪里成为美国文化的一部分。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It was 100 years ago this week that the bottle earned a patent.
lines.translation: 就在本周之前的一百年前，这种瓶子获得了专利。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: By World War II, Coke bottle sales had ballooned into billions.
lines.translation: 到第二次世界大战时，可口可乐瓶装产品的销量已经达到数十亿瓶。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Americans mostly consume Coke out of aluminum or plastic today, but the glass bottle remains a symbol of America that's readily recognized around the world.
lines.translation: 如今，美国人饮用可口可乐时主要使用铝罐或塑料瓶，但这种玻璃瓶仍然是美国的象征，在世界各地都很容易被认出。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 9-11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题9 -11是基于你刚才听到的段落

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.translation: 9. 国家

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What does the passage say appears in almost all ads for Coca-Cola?
lines.translation: 话语上说 几乎所有可口可乐广告 都写了些什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question 10.
lines.translation: 问题10。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Why did the Coca-Cola company decide to have special packaging designed?
lines.translation: 为什么可口可乐公司决定设计特殊包装物?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question 11.
lines.translation: 问题11。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What do we learn about the Coca-Cola bottle designed by the root glass company?
lines.translation: 我们该如何了解根玻璃公司设计的可口可乐瓶子?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Passage 2.
lines.translation: 通行证2。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Research shows that a few moments of conversation with a stranger creates a measurable improvement in mood.
lines.translation: 研究表明，与陌生人进行短暂的交谈能使情绪得到明显的改善。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But most of us are reluctant to start these conversations because we presume the opposite.
lines.translation: 但我们大多数人都不愿意开启这些对话，因为我们以为情况恰恰相反。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In an experiment, commuters who talked to nearby strangers found their commute more enjoyable than those who didn't.
lines.translation: 在一项实验中，与身边的陌生人交谈的通勤者发现，他们的通勤过程比那些没有交谈的人更令人愉快。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They were asked to predict whether they'd enjoy the commute more if they conversed with other people.
lines.translation: 他们被要求预测如果与他人交谈，自己是否会更享受通勤。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Intriguingly, most expected the more solitary experience to be more pleasurable.
lines.translation: 有趣的是，大多数人预想独处的体验会更令人愉快。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Why is this?
lines.translation: 为什么会这样？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Social anxiety appears to be the problem.
lines.translation: 社交焦虑似乎是问题所在。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: People's reluctance to start conversations with nearby strangers comes partly from "underestimating others' interest in connecting".
lines.translation: 人们不愿意与身边的陌生人开启对话，部分原因在于“低估了他人建立联系的兴趣”。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The sad thing is that people presume that a nearby stranger doesn't want to converse and don't start a conversation.
lines.translation: 令人遗憾的是，人们假定身边的陌生人不想交谈，因而没有开启对话。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Only those who forced themselves to chat because it was required by the experiment found out what a pleasant experience it could be.
lines.translation: 只有那些因实验要求而强迫自己聊天的人，才发现这会是多么令人愉快的体验。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Human beings are social animals.
lines.translation: 人类是社交动物。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Those who misunderstand the impact of social interactions may not, in some contexts, be social enough for their own well-being.
lines.translation: 那些误解社交互动影响的人，在某些情况下可能为了自身的幸福感而表现得不够合群。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You should be chatting with the strangers you encounter.
lines.translation: 你应该与遇到的陌生人聊天。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You may occasionally have a negative encounter that might stick in your memory.
lines.translation: 你偶尔可能会遇到不愉快的经历，并且可能会留在记忆中。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This is because the human brain is biased to dwell on negative events.
lines.translation: 这是因为人类大脑倾向于关注负面事件。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But starting conversations with strangers is still well worth the risk of rejection.
lines.translation: 但冒着被拒绝的风险与陌生人开启对话依然非常值得。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It may surprise you that conversing with strangers will make them happier too.
lines.translation: 与陌生人交谈也会让他们感到更高兴，这可能会让你感到惊讶。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The pleasure of connection seems contagious.
lines.translation: 建立联系的乐趣似乎具有传染性。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: People who are talked to have equally positive experiences as those who initiate a conversation.
lines.translation: 被搭话的人与发起对话的人拥有同样积极的体验。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Why does a negative encounter with strangers stick in one's memory?
lines.translation: 为什么和陌生人的负面遭遇 总是停留在记忆中呢?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question 15.
lines.translation: 问题15。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What does the passage say the pleasure of connection seems to be?
lines.translation: 段落上说连接的乐趣是什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Section C, directions.
lines.translation: C节,方向。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In this section you'll hear three recordings of lectures or talks followed by three or four questions.
lines.translation: 在本节中,你们将听到三段演讲或谈话录音,然后三四个问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The recordings will be played only once.
lines.translation: 录音只播放一次。

lines.text: you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A
lines.translation: 听到一个问题 您必须从四个A类选择中 选择最好的答案

lines.speaker: 听力原声

lines.translation: B、C和D,然后在答复表1中用单行横线标出相应的字母,横划

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The Caribbean islands are divided into two worlds, a rich one and a poor one.
lines.translation: 加勒比海诸岛被分为两个世界：一个富裕的世界和一个贫困的世界。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This tropical region's economy is based mainly on farming.
lines.translation: 这个热带地区的经济主要以农业为基础。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Farmers are of two types.
lines.translation: 农民有两种类型。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: One is the plantation owner who may have hundreds of thousands of acres.
lines.translation: 一种是拥有数十万英亩土地的种植园主。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In contrast, the small cultivator is working only a few acres of land.
lines.translation: 相比之下，小农只耕种几英亩土地。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Most visitors to the Caribbean are rich, like the plantation owner.
lines.translation: 大多数到加勒比海旅游的游客都很富有，就像种植园主一样。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They do not realize or do not want to realize that many farm families barely managed to get by on what they grow.
lines.translation: 他们没有意识到，或者不愿意识到，许多农民家庭仅靠自己种植的东西勉强维持生计。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The Caribbean produces many things.
lines.translation: 加勒比海地区生产许多东西。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Sugar is the main product.
lines.translation: 糖是主要产品。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Other export crops are tobacco, coffee, bananas, spices and citrus fruits, such as orange, lemon or grapefruit.
lines.translation: 其他出口作物包括烟草、咖啡、香蕉、香料和柑橘类水果，如橙子、柠檬或葡萄柚。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: From the West Indies also come oil, mineral pitch and many forest products.
lines.translation: 西印度群岛还出产石油、矿物沥青和许多林产品。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Jamaica's aluminum ore supplies are the world's largest.
lines.translation: 牙买加的铝矿储量居世界首位。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Oil comes from Trinidad, Aruba and Curacao.
lines.translation: 石油产自特立尼达、阿鲁巴和库拉索。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But for many of the smaller islands, sugar is the only export.
lines.translation: 但对许多较小的岛屿来说，糖是唯一的出口产品。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Rum, a strong alcoholic drink, which is distilled from sugar cane, is also an export.
lines.translation: 朗姆酒是一种从甘蔗中蒸馏出来的烈性酒，也是一种出口产品。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The world's best rum comes from this area.
lines.translation: 世界上最好的朗姆酒产自这一地区。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Local kinds vary from the light rums of Puerto Rico to the heavier darker rums of Barbados and Jamaica.
lines.translation: 当地朗姆酒的种类各不相同，从波多黎各的淡色朗姆酒，到巴巴多斯和牙买加较为浓烈、颜色较深的朗姆酒都有。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: American tourists enjoy stocking up on inexpensive high quality Caribbean rum while they're on vacation.
lines.translation: 美国游客在度假期间喜欢购买价格低廉而品质优良的加勒比朗姆酒。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In Curacao, the well-known liquor of that name is made from the thick outer skin of a native orange.
lines.translation: 在库拉索，以该地闻名的酒名命名的利口酒，是用当地一种橙子的厚外皮制成的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Ever since America's colonial days, the Caribbean islands have been favorite places to visit.
lines.translation: 自美国殖民时期以来，加勒比海诸岛一直是人们喜爱的旅游地。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Since World War II, tourism has increased rapidly.
lines.translation: 第二次世界大战以来，旅游业迅速发展。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Because great numbers of people go there, the islanders have built elaborate resorts, developed harbors and airfields, improved the beaches and have expanded sea and air routes.
lines.translation: 由于前往那里的人数众多，岛民修建了精致的度假胜地，开发了港口和机场，改善了海滩，并扩展了海上和空中航线。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Everything is at the resort-hotel, beach, shopping and recreation.
lines.translation: 度假酒店、海滩、购物和娱乐一应俱全。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The vacationer never has any reason to explore the island.
lines.translation: 度假者完全没有理由去探索这座岛屿。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: As in most places, those who have money live well indeed.
lines.translation: 和大多数地方一样，有钱人确实过着优裕的生活。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Those who don't have money live at various levels of poverty.
lines.translation: 没有钱的人则处于不同程度的贫困之中。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But here the poor greatly outnumber the wealthy.
lines.translation: 但在这里，穷人的数量远远超过富人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: A visitor will find rich people living in apartments or Spanish houses at the seaside or in the countryside.
lines.translation: 游客会看到富人住在海边或乡间的公寓里，或者住在西班牙式房屋中。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Their servants might include a cook, a maid, and a nurse for their children.
lines.translation: 他们的仆人可能包括厨师、女佣和照顾孩子的护士。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Most of the people live well below the poverty level.
lines.translation: 大多数人的生活水平远低于贫困线。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In towns, they live crowded together in tiny houses.
lines.translation: 在城镇里，他们拥挤地住在狭小的房屋中。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Islanders make the best they can of what they have.
lines.translation: 岛民们尽可能利用自己所拥有的一切。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Their homes are quite shabby.
lines.translation: 他们的住房相当破旧。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Sadly, most tourists never see the side of the Caribbean.
lines.translation: 令人遗憾的是，大多数游客从未见过加勒比海的这一面。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What does the speaker say about the economy of the Caribbean islands?
lines.translation: 发言者对加勒比岛屿的经济怎么说?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question 17.
lines.translation: 问题17。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What is the main product of the Caribbean islands?
lines.translation: 加勒比岛屿的主要产品是什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question 18.
lines.translation: 问题18。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What do we learn about the majority of people in the Caribbean islands?
lines.translation: 我们如何了解加勒比岛屿上大多数人的情况?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Recording 2.
lines.translation: 记录2。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Talk to anyone who is a generation or two older and they would most likely comment that children are more spoiled these days.
lines.translation: 和比自己年长一两代的人交谈，他们很可能会说，如今的孩子更加娇生惯养了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: No one wants to have or be around demanding, selfish and spoiled children, those who get bad-tempered or silently brood when they are not given everything they want immediately.
lines.translation: 没有人愿意拥有或和那些要求过多、自私且被宠坏的孩子相处；当他们不能立即得到自己想要的一切时，就会变得脾气暴躁或闷闷不乐。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Paradoxically, the parents of such children encourage this demanding behavior in the mistaken belief that by giving their children everything they can their children will be happy.
lines.translation: 矛盾的是，这类孩子的父母却错误地认为，只要尽可能满足孩子的一切要求，孩子就会感到幸福，于是反而助长了这种索取无度的行为。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In the short term, perhaps they are right.
lines.translation: 短期来看，他们或许是对的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But in the longer term, such children end up lonely, dependent, chronically dissatisfied and resentful of the parents who tried so hard to please them.
lines.translation: 但从长远来看，这些孩子最终会变得孤独、依赖他人、长期不满，并对那些竭力取悦他们的父母心怀怨恨。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Undoubtedly parents want to raise happy children who are confident, capable and likable rather than spoiled and miserable.
lines.translation: 毫无疑问，父母都希望把孩子培养成幸福、自信、有能力且讨人喜欢的人，而不是被宠坏又不快乐的人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: One factor hindering this is that parents can't or don't spend enough quality time with their kids, and substitute this deficit with toys, games, gadgets and the like.
lines.translation: 阻碍这一目标的一个因素是，父母无法或没有花足够的高质量时间陪伴孩子，于是用玩具、游戏、电子设备之类的东西来弥补这一不足。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Rather than getting material things, children need parents' devoted attention.
lines.translation: 孩子需要的不是物质上的东西，而是父母全心全意的关注。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The quantity of time spent together is less important than the content of that time.
lines.translation: 共同相处的时间长短并不如相处时光的内容重要。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Instead of instantly satisfying their wishes, parents should help them work out a plan to earn things they'd like to have.
lines.translation: 父母不应立即满足孩子的愿望，而应帮助他们制定计划，通过努力获得自己想要的东西。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This teaches them to value the effort as well as what it achieves.
lines.translation: 这能教会他们既重视努力本身，也重视努力所取得的成果。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Allow them to enjoy anticipation.
lines.translation: 让孩子享受期待的过程。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Numerous psychological studies have demonstrated that children who learn to wait for things they desire are more likely to succeed in a number of ways later in life.
lines.translation: 大量心理学研究表明，学会等待自己渴望的事物的孩子，日后更有可能在许多方面取得成功。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: One famous experiment in the 1960s involved 3- to 6-year-old children.
lines.translation: 20世纪60年代进行的一项著名实验以3至6岁的儿童为对象。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They were given a choice between receiving a small reward, such as a cookie, immediately, or if they waited 15 minutes, they could have two.
lines.translation: 他们可以选择立即得到一份小奖励，例如一块饼干；也可以等待15分钟，这样就能得到两块。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Follow up studies have found that those who chose to delay satisfaction are now more academically successful, have greater self-worth, and even tend to be healthier.
lines.translation: 后续研究发现，那些选择延迟满足的孩子，如今在学业上更加成功，自我价值感更强，而且往往也更加健康。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If they fail, children should be encouraged to keep trying rather than to give up if they really want the desired result.
lines.translation: 如果失败了，只要孩子确实想要达到预期的结果，就应鼓励他们继续尝试，而不是放弃。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This teaches them how to handle and recover from disappointment, which is associated with greater success and satisfaction academically, financially and in personal relationships.
lines.translation: 这能教会他们如何应对失望并从中恢复，而这与他们在学业、经济状况和个人关系方面取得更大的成功与满足感有关。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And lastly, parents should encourage their children to look at life from other points of view, as well as their own.
lines.translation: 最后，父母还应鼓励孩子从其他人的角度以及自己的角度看待生活。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This teaches them to be understanding of and sympathetic towards others—qualities sure to take them a long way in life.
lines.translation: 这能教会他们理解和同情他人，而这些品质必将让他们在人生道路上受益匪浅。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题19至21是基于你刚才听到的录音

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question 19.
lines.translation: 问题19。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What will happen to children?
lines.translation: 儿童会怎样?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If they always get immediate satisfaction.
lines.translation: 如果他们总是得到 立即满意。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What may prevent parents from raising confident and capable children?
lines.translation: 是什么可以阻止父母抚养自信和有能力的孩子?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question 21.
lines.translation: 问题21

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Why should children be encouraged to keep trying when they fail?
lines.translation: 为什么要鼓励儿童在失败时继续尝试呢?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.translation: 3 个

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's not hard to mess up an interview.
lines.translation: 搞砸面试并不难

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It is not hard to mess up an interview.
lines.translation: 面试出错并不难。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Most people feel nervous sitting across from a hiring manager, answering questions that effectively open themselves up for judgment.
lines.translation: 大多数人坐在招聘经理对面，回答那些实际上会让自己暴露在评判之下的问题时，都会感到紧张。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And your chances of being more carefully considered for the job can quickly go downhill just by saying the wrong thing at the wrong time.
lines.translation: 仅仅因为在错误的时间说了错误的话，你被更认真地考虑录用的机会就可能迅速下降。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The most obvious thing not to do is complain.
lines.translation: 最明显应该避免的事情就是抱怨。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Employers want to hire positive people.
lines.translation: 雇主希望招聘积极乐观的人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Talking about a previous job negatively raises concerns that you might be difficult to manage, or you might be someone that blames management for your own poor performance.
lines.translation: 负面谈论上一份工作会引发担忧，让人觉得你可能难以管理，或者你可能是那种把自己的糟糕表现归咎于管理层的人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Don't say that you've moved around in jobs because you haven't found the right fit or feel that you were not challenged enough.
lines.translation: 不要说你换过多份工作是因为一直没有找到合适的岗位，或者觉得自己没有得到足够的挑战。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Statements like these will make you sound aimless and lost.
lines.translation: 这样的说法会让你听起来漫无目的、迷失方向。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: An interviewer may well think, why would this role be any different for you?
lines.translation: 面试官很可能会想：这个职位对你来说又会有什么不同呢？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You will probably leave here in six months.
lines.translation: 你大概六个月后就会离开这里。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It also begs the question of what type of relationship you had with your manager.
lines.translation: 这也会让人不禁思考你和经理之间的关系如何。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It doesn't sound like you had open communication with him or her.
lines.translation: 听起来，你似乎没有与他或她进行坦诚的沟通。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Managers usually love people who can self-sustain and enable growth through taking initiative, who are strong at following through their work, and who bring ideas and solutions to the table.
lines.translation: 经理通常很喜欢那些能够自我驱动、通过主动采取行动促进成长、善于把工作贯彻到底，并且能够提出想法和解决方案的人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If you were in a management or leadership position, when discussing your current role, never take all the credit for accomplishments or achievements.
lines.translation: 如果你曾担任管理或领导职位，在谈论当前职位时，绝不要把所有功劳或成就都归于自己。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Emphasize your team and how through their talents, your vision was realized.
lines.translation: 要突出你的团队，以及你是如何凭借他们的才能实现自己的愿景的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Most successful leaders know that they are only as good as their team.
lines.translation: 大多数成功的领导者都知道，自己的能力取决于团队的表现。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And acknowledging this in an interview will go a long way towards suggesting that you might be the right person for the position you are applying for.
lines.translation: 在面试中承认这一点，将大大有助于表明你可能正是所申请职位的合适人选。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Lastly, have a good idea of what your role will be and try and convey the idea that you're flexible.
lines.translation: 最后，要清楚了解自己的职责，并努力传达出你具有灵活性。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Asking what your role will be suggests you will limit yourself purely to what is expected of you.
lines.translation: 询问自己的职责是什么，会让人觉得你打算把自己严格限制在他人对你的期望之内。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In reality, your role is whatever you make of it.
lines.translation: 实际上，你的职责取决于你如何发挥。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This is especially true in small companies, where the ability to adapt and take on new responsibilities is highly valued.
lines.translation: 在小公司中尤其如此，因为适应变化并承担新的责任的能力备受重视。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And this is equally important if you're just starting out.
lines.translation: 如果你刚刚开始职业生涯，这一点同样重要。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Entry level interviewees would do well to demonstrate a broad set of skills in most interviews.
lines.translation: 对于初级职位的面试者来说，在大多数面试中展示广泛的技能组合会很有帮助。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's important to have a wide skill set as many startups and small companies are moving really fast.
lines.translation: 拥有多方面的技能非常重要，因为许多初创公司和小公司发展得非常快。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Employers are looking for candidates that are intelligent and can quickly adapt and excel in a growing company.
lines.translation: 雇主正在寻找聪明、能够迅速适应并在不断成长的公司中取得优异表现的候选人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题22至25是基于你刚才听到的录音

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What does the speaker say can easily prevent an interviewee from getting a job?
lines.translation: 发言者说什么可以轻易阻止受访者找到工作?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question 23 What should the interviewee avoid doing in an interview?
lines.translation: 问题23 受访者在接受访谈时如何避免这样做?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question 24 What kind of employees do companies like to recruit?
lines.translation: 问题24:公司喜欢招聘什么样的雇员?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question 25 What is especially important for those working in a small company?
lines.translation: 问题25 哪些对于在小公司工作的人特别重要?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That's the end of listening comprehension.
lines.translation: 听觉理解到此结束
